newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus market inches up on high volumes.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus market inches up on high volumes.

text.p: Cyprus's stock exchange inched up 0.65 percent on Wednesday on high trading volumes as institutional investors moved in, analysts said.

"People are beginning to stop dithering and they are moving into the market, more importantly the institutions are moving in" said Nicolas Severis, an economist and chairman of Sigma Severis Athientis Ltd, a member of the Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE).
The CSE index, set at 100 points, closed at 77.10 on Wednesday, up 1.72 percent from the market close on Friday. It has a PE ratio of around 16, said Severis.

"People were dithering because they thought the market was going to go lower, but it did not," said Severis, who added the market found resistance at the 73.80 mark the index fell to on January 31, its all-time low.
Analysts have now turned their attention to the preliminary results of 1996 due to be announced by the Bank of Cyprus on Friday, the island's largest banking institution.
Severis said the results would be the "first key element" to short-term prospects of the market.
Banking stocks closed at 87.71, gaining 2.02 percent from Friday's close. The closing price for Bank of Cyprus fully paid shares was 326 cents, from 320.5 on Friday.
The Cyprus Popular Bank, which is due to announce its own preliminary 1996 results in a week's time, closed on its fully paid shares at 318, up seven cents from Friday's close.
The Hellenic Bank gained eight cents, closing at 264.5, while the Universal Savings Bank closed at 166.5 from 157.5 on Friday.
Universal Life Insurance gained three cents, closing at 406. Paneuropean closed at 108.5, up four cents while Interamerican Insurance closed at 98.5 from 95.5 last week.
Vassiliko Cement closed at 136.5, gaining half a cent, while beer and wine manufacturers Keo was trading at 101.5, down two cents from Friday.
Retailers Woolworth was trading at 78.5, up two cents. Last week the company announced an expansion project to build a new department store complex in the Engomi suburb of Nicosia.
